static_traits.name: Lin Jie
static_traits.educational_background: Currently studying for a bachelor's degree
static_traits.social_status: Has a girlfriend and several veteran peers to talk with, but believes they may not necessarily fully understand the academic pressure faced
static_traits.medical_history: No similar academic anxiety appeared before; no prior psychotherapy/counseling history; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, able to self-reflect on cognitive patterns; highly cooperative, sincere tone; nervous but controlled emotions

basic_info.main_problem: After getting a poor grade on an assignment, I feel overwhelmed and anxious about academic performance, fearing failure and being dismissed from school. This fear has grown stronger since the event, troubling me almost daily, especially before exams or when receiving grades, already affecting my motivation and confidence.
basic_info.core_demands: The fear of failure and its impact on my mental health and academic performance prompted me to seek counseling support.
growth_experiences: After entering school as a veteran, felt strong pressure 'to perform well' from the very start (occurring before this difference event).
Family-of-origin information: father once served in the military.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough / not suited for this study
My worth depends on grades and others' expectations (failure equals disappointing my family)

special_situations.event: Receiving a poor grade on an assignment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one assignment goes badly, it means I am not suited for this study and will fail courses next
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling study, seeking help from professors, using relaxation techniques to reduce anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will soon be expelled from school / fail courses

special_situations.event: Before exams or while waiting for results
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If this exam does not go well, it proves I will fail and disappoint my family
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Increasing review intensity and trying relaxation techniques, while repeatedly envisioning the worst outcome in order to 'be prepared'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time will most likely be bad; I might fail the course

special_situations.event: Thinking about family's expectations and judgment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach high standards, I will disappoint my family, showing I am no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Studying harder, seeking help from professors to meet others' expectations

special_situations.event: Reviewing an individual setback when self-assessing ability (e.g. one poor grade)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as there is one failure, it proves I am simply no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Develops thoughts of giving up to avoid the blow of failing again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not cut out for this / I am not suited to study this

core_conflict.wish: Longing to gain recognition and peace through stable academic performance, especially being accepted and affirmed by family
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure, being negated and disappointing family, thus being seen as unworthy or not good enough
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of failure and criticism by doubling efforts and imagining the worst outcome in advance

object_relations.self_representation: A student who may fail and disappoint important others
object_relations.object_representation: Family members/significant others with high expectations of oneself who may be disappointed

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing 'what one bad grade means' or being asked about views on failure
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to interpret one setback as 'total failure', as if there is no middle ground
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Describing self and outcomes with absolutist words (e.g. 'certainly', 'all', 'completely no good'), tense tone, ignoring partial successes or room for improvement.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When approaching exams or waiting for results to be announced
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes imagining the worst case in advance can 'prepare' oneself to avoid the blow
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeatedly describing worst outcomes and contingency plans, using the pattern 'if this does not work out it is all over', speaking slightly fast, focusing on future threats rather than present evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking about family expectations or being asked about worries over family reactions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning possible outward disappointment and dissatisfaction against the self, reinforcing self-blame and self-denial
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressions dominated by self-blame and self-belittlement (e.g. 'it is all because I am not good', 'I disappointed them'), lowering self-worth, guilty tone.

manifestations: Feeling the girlfriend and veteran peers cannot fully understand the academic pressure and situation
The role transition from military to campus brings a sense of adaptation gap
outcomes: Disrupted sleep rhythm and decreased attention

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and introspection, involving excessive self-restriction and self-reproach, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequently evaluating oneself with self-blame and absolutist ways (e.g. 'I am not suited', 'I will fail')
Treats a single setback as proof of overall ability, lowers the sense of self-worth

positive_force: Proactively seeking support (asking professors for help, using relaxation techniques)
Having some self-observation and cognitive reflection ability (able to identify 'jumping to conclusions' and 'catastrophizing')
Willing to try behavioral experiments and cognitive restructuring
Having some social support (girlfriend and veteran peers)
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, and overgeneralization are significant
Sensitive to external evaluation; worries about disappointing family
Persistent worry causing impaired sleep and attention
Decreased motivation after setbacks with emerging giving-up tendencies

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated worry and catastrophizing anticipation related to academics
antecedent: Receiving a poor grade on an assignment
Waiting for grades to be published
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing cognitions about failure and worries about disappointing family reinforcing threat appraisal
target_behavior.function: Gaining a 'sense of control' over uncertainty through advance worrying, trying to avoid failing again
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep disturbance, decreased attention and worsened anxiety, further impairing academic performance

target_behavior.behavior: Decreased learning motivation and emerging thoughts of giving up
antecedent: Experiencing 'I will fail / not suited' automatic thoughts after setbacks
Making extreme judgments about one's ability when reviewing an individual poor grade
target_behavior.core_reason: Helplessness and self-denial caused by black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential failure and negative evaluation, relieving anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Declining learning engagement and grades, plus pressure on the intimate relationship (with girlfriend)
